column5: Claim quotes Waite's "logical succession" of the high degrees; linked p.257 states it ("The logical order and succession of the High Degrees—The Royal Arch"; "How it restores the lost secret"). Target p.264 ("It is these mysteries that are rediscovered in the Royal Arch degree") holds only the restoration half. The move leaves a page that says it.

Mardana list item. Target p.2: "Grinding with the specified medicines along with very sour kanjika is called mardana; it destroys impurities." Linked p.3 covers murchana/utthapana/patana, not mardana.
Bound mercury stable in fire. Target p.217: "it remains stable when held in the midst of fire; this is the characteristic of the Bound Form". Linked p.216 only names the states.

Ifa and the Yoruba political order. Target p.127: "the connection between Ifa, the first Oni, and these foundational walls is self-evident." Linked p.126 describes the Ogboni and the four walls, with no Ifa link stated.

Secret Teachings as a single-volume distillation of Hermetic/Rosicrucian thought. Target (Lost Keys p.128, publisher's ad for the Encyclopedic Outline): "Between the covers of a single volume have been gathered those priceless secrets". Linked (Lectures back cover) calls it a "masterpiece of symbolic philosophy" but is about the companion volume. Both partly; the target is closer.

Murchana definition. Target Rasaratnasamuccaya p.244: "grinding mercury ... until it ... becomes a paste is called murchana. This indeed destroys the defects associated with tin, lead, and arsenic." Linked Rasa-Jala-Nidhi p.153 is the 13th process with no definition. But the answer's prose still says "In the Rasa Jala Nidhi", so after the cross-book move the sentence names the wrong book.

AGLA as a notarikon of Atah Gibor Le-olam Adonai. Target Agrippa III p.46: "the name Agla is drawn from this verse of the Holy Scripture: Atah Gibor Le-olam Adonai". Linked Key of Solomon p.75 only invokes AGLA; the expansion there is our translator's <note>, not the source.

Unison: a plucked string sets a same-pitched string vibrating. Linked p.551 states it: "the strings of the other instruments that happen to be at the unison of said strings or voices will respond to them ... without touching the strings". Target p.550 states only the stopped-string corollary. The move leaves a page that says it.

A range citation, "Página 328-330", under a three-bullet summary. Linked p.328 states the pallor and the "miserable spectacle of unnatural enjoyment"; target p.330 states the appetite and "a painful death". Moving it drops half the support, and moveIn rewrites the label to "Página 330-330".

Poimandres as "a vision of the creation of the universe". The only words that say this on target Patrizi p.219 are OUR translator's <note> ("The title of the first book of the Corpus Hermeticum, which describes a vision of the creation"), not Patrizi. The move swaps the book on the strength of an editorial note. Linked Ficino p.10 does not state it either: the right action was drop.

Love charm with butterbur and foxglove. Both pages state it: linked p.60 (the Gaelic page, translated) has "Take with you the 'peaked canopy' butterbur ... 'priest's cap' foxglove", and target p.61 (Carmichael's English) has "Take with you the 'pointed canopy'". The move goes to the English facing page; no loss.

Women: "ataques histéricos", "ictericia incurable", "barrenza". Linked Onania p.36: "It is frequently the cause of hysterick fits ... what it produces more often than either is barrenness". Target Tissot p.57: "fits of hysteria or frightful vapors, to incurable jaundice". Each holds two of the three. The move swaps the book the prose names ("Onania") and loses barrenness: no gain.

Rasalinga as the highest form of Shiva, with a blockquote. Target p.44: "The merit that is obtained from worshipping countless other Shivalingas is surely obtained through the worship of this single Rasalinga ... There is nothing higher in this world than the worship of the Rasalinga." Linked p.58 names the rasalinga only in passing.

Ma'at, daughter of Ra, with the feather as her emblem. Target p.199: "Maat, the goddess of the unchangeable laws of heaven and the daughter of Ra ... She wears the feather—which is symbolic of maat—on her head". Linked p.198 has only "the daughter of Rā", with no feather.

Elisha's "double portion" of Elijah's spirit, cited to Visscher. Linked p.177 states it: "on Elisha his Spirit has rested doubly". The move takes the link to another book (Arabic Bible, 2 Kgs 2:9) on a 5-word span.

Weyer: melancholy; "the devil ... dazzled their imagination with phantoms". Linked p.153 states the main clause: "so that the Devil can dazzle their imagination with various phantoms". Target p.152 has only "they are tormented by melancholic diseases". The move leaves the page that holds the claim's own words.

Bureus as the father of Swedish runology. Linked p.12 states it: "Johan Bureus ... has the honor of having first brought to life the study of runestones ... can therefore be considered the first true antiquarian researcher". Target p.13 adds only "Bureus had a few hundred such stones depicted". The move leaves the better page.

A stitched blockquote across two pages. "Heaven is in the heart. They will look for it in vain who look elsewhere" is on linked p.185; "The Kingdom of Heaven is man's Home: and it is here and now, it is in his own heart" is on target p.188. The move trades one half for the other; the right fix cites both pages.

Bahya-druti (external liquefaction). Target Rasaprakasasudhakara p.9: "internal liquefaction, external liquefaction, and the digestion of the liquefied substance". The list on linked Rasa-Jala-Nidhi p.74 has garbha-druti but no external liquefaction.

Pushpaka: built by Vishvakarma for Brahma, then Kuvera's, then taken by Ravana. Target p.48: "It had been built in the heavens by Viçwakarmā for the creator god Brahmā himself. Later, Kuvera obtained it ... but the Rākshasa chief took possession of it". On linked p.44 it appears only in our <note>.

The stone repeatedly calls King Ptolemy V 'beloved of Ptah'. Linked p.173 states it: "nesu-bat, King of the South and North, Ptolemy, ever-living, beloved of Ptah". The fixer said keep, but its span added "the" ("Ptolemy, the ever-living"), so code dropped it as drop_unverified.

Apple grafted on a plane tree gives red apples, on a poplar white. Linked p.183 makes apples red by steam from ditches or by "prepare the apple tree under a matzi"; nothing on grafting onto plane or poplar.
Epictetus: focus on what lies within our will. The link (a title link carrying p.545) lands on the index ("Desires in our own power, i. 4, 114"), which points elsewhere and does not state it.

Hermes as Thoth+Hermes; the Corpus written in the 2nd–3rd c. CE and rediscovered in the Renaissance. Patrizi p.219 gives the 36,525 books and the two surviving works. The dating and the synthesis appear nowhere but our <note>s.
Madhura covers meats, fats and milk, "unctuous, heavy, building". Linked p.414 only enumerates the two- and three-taste combinations ("Sweet, acid and saline; ..."), not food classes.

A stimulant user's aura "becomes sticky" and draws entities that feed on anxiety and fear. Linked p.33 has elementals that "gather round places where liquor is sold, and feed on its exhalations, and are attracted round him by the effluvia of his own drink-sodden body". The topic is close, but sticky aura, anxiety/fear feeders and personality change are not stated.
Lilith seducing men in dreams. Linked Kabbala denudata II p.245 is letter-permutation tables (TzG | DH | VZ ...) under "Chapter XXIV. Persona of Daath"; no Lilith.

Most scholars consider it a pseudo-Agrippa text. Linked p.1 is the 1559 title page ("Henry Cornelius Agrippa's Fourth Book on Occult Philosophy, or on Ceremonial Magic"). It shows the book but not the attribution claim the link carries.

A blockquote: "to join our assembly you must perceive this light ... you cannot see us unless we wish". Linked Vaughan p.67 (Anthroposophia Theomagica, the soul's powers out of the body) does not contain it, nor the word "light".

In Papus's system the number 2 represents Binah, the feminine receptive vessel. Linked p.165 states the receptive-feminine half: "all the passive meanings derived from the 'Binary' (the number two) ... the 'Woman'" and "a sacred dwelling or a divine recipient". It does not name Binah. Partly stated, so the marker "(not from the library's pages)" overstates.
Ruel: pick apples by hand and store them in barley straw or vine leaves. Linked p.533 is apple varieties (lanata, septiana, "conditiua, which are stored in jars"), with no picking or straw.

Music makes the spiritus "thinner, faster and warmer", driving out black bile. Linked Kircher p.968 states it: "the spirits, which, being rendered thinner, swifter, and warmer, dissipate and attenuate or mitigate those humors". The fixer said keep, but copied a span from elsewhere, so code dropped it as drop_unverified.

Tzolk'in, a 260-day calendar. Each day was a 'burden' carried by a god. Linked Paris Codex p.16 is only image description ("a grid of 20 hieroglyphic blocks ... columns of red and black numerical notation"). It shows grids but states nothing about the Tzolk'in or burdens.

The ingredients are "sandalwood, saffron, musk and camphor". The fragmentary linked p.1 has them: "with flower, sandalwood, musk, and saffron, purified indeed ... camphor's", and honey. Not stated: the paste applied to the body for fragrance. The ingredient line, the bullet's main content, is on the page.

Their descendants still form a prestigious social and religious elite in modern Senegal and Mauritania. Linked Delafosse p.254 covers the Toucouleurs' mixed origins and naturalized Tòrobé, with nothing on a present-day elite.

Agrippa's Book II figures of the human body inscribed in geometric shapes. Linked p.322 is that passage: "the distance between the feet ... will form an equilateral triangle; and with the center placed at the navel, a circle drawn around will touch the extremities of the hands and feet." The planetary alignment is not stated, but the cited figure is.

Galen: warm dry skins are porous (araiotes) and burn perfume quickly. Linked Kühn I p.618 uses araiotes the other way, "if the part is easily chilled, it indicates either coldness or araiotes", and says nothing on perfume.

Ik: governed by the God of Wind, a 'T' glyph representing life and breath. Linked Cortesianus p.13 shows Ik in the day-sign grid and "a large, boxed Ik (Wind) glyph". The page shows the glyph but states nothing on the god, the T-shape or breath.
Ma'at "stands at the prow of the solar barque". Linked Ani facsimile p.24 is the judgment scene (the feather of Ma'at in the right scale); no barque.

specific sounds are believed to sever the 'bonds' of mercury's volatility, transforming it into khotaka or bhasmasuta. Linked Rasarnava p.217 defines both states ("when its flickering volatility is destroyed, this is the characteristic of Ash-Mercury") but has nothing on sound or mantra, the sentence's own claim.
